done_when: The worker brief lets a worker change a file outside its Scope that the change needs, naming each such file and why in its handoff, and the review reports only outside-Scope files the work doesn't need; workers still stop for a one-way step, a security question, a new moving part or contradicting Done-when items. The brief and the review ask for an end-to-end test only for items that change runtime behaviour; settings, docs, deletions and test-only items are proven by the check the item names. The brief tells workers to name new test files after the behaviour they prove, never after the fix's slug.

findings.body: The changed conditional rule is followed by unconditional instructions in this same file: line 32 requires an HTTP test for an item with no UI, and line 50 requires a Playwright test for every user-facing item. The worker brief points workers to this testing convention at src/forge/templates/brief.md:174-175. A settings or documentation item can therefore still be assigned an end-to-end test instead of its named check. These two instructions are new evidence beyond the unconditional lines addressed in the previous review.
findings.title: Not done: Nonruntime items still trigger end-to-end test rules

findings.body: This test checks that the conditional sentence appears in the generated brief, but it passes while src/forge/templates/conventions/testing.md:32 and :50 still impose unconditional HTTP and Playwright tests. The test named for asking end-to-end tests only for runtime behaviour therefore misses a real contradiction in the guidance workers are directed to read. Extend the command-level check to cover that guidance.
findings.title: Not done: Test the complete nonruntime testing guidance

why: Workers stop and ask before every file outside their Scope, even a caller or type file the change plainly needs, and the brief demands an end-to-end test for every item even for docs, settings, deletions and test-only changes, so workers and reviews waste rounds
